newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stock market liquidity to rise on automation.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stock market liquidity to rise on automation.

text.p: The Colombo Stock Exchange, which began screen-based trading trials this week, will see an improvement in share liquidity once the system becomes fully operational in July, brokers and officials said on Friday.

"A good part of an average 20 percent of daily transactions which did not get executed under the old open outcry system, are already starting to get done," said Sudarshan Ahangama of John Keells Stock Brokers.
"Trading has improved because there is no lag between the time a client gives an order and it is carried out. There is also more information on the depth of the market," he added.
Brokers said Colombo's perennial problem of low market liquidity, where only about 100 of the 238 listed firms were regularly traded, was compounded by bottlenecks in the manual trading system.
"Of course, the real material improvement in liquidity will come only when more shares of more firms are regularly traded," said another broker.
Though the open-outcry system is no longer in use, broking houses still have to place their orders with brokers on the floor by phone, who then inject the orders into the exchange's main system.
Officials said brokers will be able to trade from their offices by the second half of July.

"The final product, which is brokers trading from their offices, will be possible only after all 15 broking firms are linked to the stock exchange through radio telephone links," said Dylan Moldrich, director general of the stock exchange.
